chunks: Saʿīd al-Aʿraj asked him about a muhrim shielding himself from the sun with a stick or with his hand.
So he said: "No, except due to an illness."

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: a person in the state of ihram
key_terms.بِعُودٍ: with a stick or piece of wood
key_terms.يَسْتَتِرُ: seeks to cover or shield himself

ai.seo_question: Can a person in ihram shield themselves from the sun with their hand or a stick?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a muhrim seeking shade from the sun while in ihram. It indicates that shielding oneself in this way is not allowed, except when there is an illness or valid medical excuse.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2683 - Saeed al-A'raj asked him about a person in the state of ihram seeking shade from the sun using a stick or their hand.
Imam (as) said: "No, except in the case of an illness."
